sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Nixa
sections.html:
Nixa owners can hire an agent, sell on their own, or take a cash offer. Cash tends to be quickest for a house that needs work, while an agent listing tends to bring the top price for one that does not. If the buyer plans to rent the house out, the city's rental inspection comes into play after closing.

Nixa grew quickly, from 12,124 residents in 2000 to 23,257 in 2020, and a lot of the housing went up during that stretch. With so much similar stock, a plain house competes on price and condition. A worn rental, a vacancy or an inherited property is a good fit for an as-is buyer who covers repairs and skips showings.

  • Agent listing: more exposure and more preparation, then a wait while the buyer's lender finishes.
  • Owner sale: you keep the agent's share and manage the contract yourself.
  • Cash purchase: the house goes as it stands, on a closing date you pick.

Judge each offer by the amount left after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not by the headline number.

The 2020 census counted 23,257 people in Nixa, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,597, which is 14.4 percent above the 2020 base. The city sits in Christian County, about six miles south of Springfield.

Roughly 27.6 percent of residents are under 18, and a three-bedroom house with a yard near an elementary school has an obvious audience. Name the school in your listing, since young families search by school. About 91.7 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier, so owners tend to stay put and few homes reach the market at any one time. That can help a well-priced listing stand out.

Nixa requires a rental unit that is at least one year old to pass an inspection before a new tenant moves in and before utilities go into the tenant's name. A seller feels it only when the buyer plans to rent the house out, but an investor buyer will ask about it.

  • Fee: $25 per inspection, paid before the visit through a link the city emails after you submit the request form.
  • Notice: 24 hours; same-day inspections are not available. Inspections run 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, in a morning or afternoon window.
  • Who can schedule: only a landlord or property manager.
  • Penalty: $50 if a tenant moves in, or receives keys, before a passed inspection. An early move-in inspection costs $75.
  • Failed inspection: 90 days to make repairs and call for a re-inspection, after which a new inspection and $25 fee apply.

The house must be empty, clean and move-in ready. The inspector looks at the roof and gutters, smoke detectors on every story, GFCI protection in bathrooms, water heater safety valves, the windows and doors, weeds above 12 inches and other items on the city's checklist. Planning and Development answers questions at (417) 725-5850.

Nixa regulates short-term residential rentals in its code, and the rules were reworked after Missouri House Bill 1662 took effect in June 2022. Call Planning and Development to learn which version applies before you advertise a house for nightly stays or sell one to someone who wants to.

The city's first ordinance dates from August 2019 and allowed such rentals only in a primary residence with a special use permit. A May 2024 staff proposal split the use into two categories. A primary residence rental needs only a city business license. A non-primary residence rental would face a ban on using accessory structures, an annual rental inspection and a 150-foot separation from other short-term rentals. An investor shopping for an Airbnb house should ask the city which of those rules is in force today.

A new owner opens a utilities account directly with Nixa Utilities. Expect a residential application, photo ID, details on every adult in the home and a deposit. Rental properties also need the passed rental inspection described above before service goes into a tenant's name.

As the seller, ask for a final reading on your closing date so service flips to the buyer the same day and you stop paying for a house you no longer own.

Christian County keeps the land records. The Recorder of Deeds office is in the Historical Courthouse at 100 W. Church Street, Room 104, in Ozark. A title company ordinarily records the deed after closing, so most sellers never go there.

The office takes walk-in, mail and electronic filings, with eRecording routed through a vendor such as iCounty Technologies. Staff cannot supply forms, notarize or give legal advice. Missouri Senate Bill 938 changed recording fees at the end of August 2026, so ask the office for the present charge. A free service at deedwatch.com emails an owner whenever a document is recorded under a registered name, which is a cheap way to watch for fraud.

Homes are assessed at 19 percent of market value. The levy comes from thirteen school districts, eight road districts, ten cities, nine fire districts and other bodies, so the districts at your address set your bill. Ask the Collector's Office in Room 101 of the courthouse for the amount and due date. Closing agents settle any tax owed at the table.

Owners who are at least 62 by December 31, 2026 may qualify for the county's Senior Citizen Real Estate Tax Credit. First-time applications open March 1, 2027 and close June 15, 2027, and the owner must have lived in the home since at least June 29, 2026 and paid the 2026 taxes. That is worth knowing if you are deciding between selling and staying.

sections.h2: Before you accept an offer in Nixa
sections.html:
1. Collect the deed, your mortgage payoff figure and the latest tax bill.
  2. Find out whether any tenant is in place and whether the rental inspection has been done.
  3. Ask each buyer for a written price, a closing date and who pays title and recording charges.
  4. Compare what each offer leaves you after repairs, commissions and carrying costs.
  5. Book the final utility reading for the closing date.

With two or three written bids side by side, the choice between speed and price gets much easier.

faqs.q: Does Nixa inspect a house when it is sold?
faqs.a: Only if the buyer plans to rent it out. Nixa's program inspects rental units before each new tenant moves in, for $25, and a landlord cannot let a tenant move in until the unit has passed.

faqs.q: What is the penalty if a tenant moves into a Nixa rental before it passes inspection?
faqs.a: $50. An early move-in inspection costs $75. A landlord who allows more than one violation can be summoned to Municipal Court.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a house in Nixa?
faqs.a: At the Christian County Recorder of Deeds in the Historical Courthouse at 100 W. Church Street, Room 104, in Ozark. Your title company can file it for you.

faqs.q: Can I run an Airbnb in my Nixa house?
faqs.a: Possibly. Nixa has short-term rental rules that were rewritten after Missouri House Bill 1662. A primary residence rental needs a city business license, and the rules for other houses may add an annual inspection and a 150-foot spacing requirement. Confirm the current version with Planning and Development.

faqs.q: How do I set up utilities after buying a house in Nixa?
faqs.a: The buyer opens an account with Nixa Utilities at 715 W Mt Vernon St with a residential application, photo ID, information on every adult living there and a deposit. Rental properties also need a passed rental inspection.
